text.content:
Characters don’t need that much Corruption for it to manifest as mutations and it’s more or less inevitable that the Characters will accumulate Corruption, especially in a setting where they encounter cultists, mutants and demons. Spellcasters in particular are on a fast track towards mental derangements and body horror. As such it’s a good idea for The GM to establish how their setting deals with Character corruption. Below are three possible themes.

Life is Short

It’s a grimdark world. If you’re not killed by a random critical wound, infection or disease, corruption will sooner or later make your Character unplayable as they will either burn at the stake or have to ee into the wilderness.

The Players should be aware that their Character’s may not last that long and see it as part of the ghastly fun of playing Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay. You can keep using the standard WFRP rules and use this supplement for generating mutated NPCs.

We Could Be Heroes

If you want to play more heroic Characters that expose corruption and fight demons over a longer period of time and still be able to socially interact with members of civilised society (like in the Enemy Within campaign), then there need to be avenues for keeping corruption and mutation in check. The GM could provide opportunities for @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.JournalEntry.NS3YGlJQxwTggjRX.JournalEntryPage.115GzWrmkD4viyy5#dark-whispers]{dark whispers}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.JournalEntry.NS3YGlJQxwTggjRX.JournalEntryPage.115GzWrmkD4viyy5#absolution]{absolution}, chaos resistance (talents, spells, magic objects etc), treatment (skilled and discrete surgeons or effective asylums) and the generosity of Shallya's priests. 

The Players should be aware that corruption is deadly and that they are expected to actively manage that risk. Use this supplement instead of the WFRP 4e rules to provide a progressive (and escalating) decline for the Characters, and the treatment section for keeping things in check.

The Heart of Darkness

You embrace corruption and work it into the theme of your story. The Character’s are doomed anti-heroes or villains as the Ruinous Powers inevitably taint their souls.  The GM will either have to find ways for them to interact with society without being immediately killed or set the scene for their adventures in a setting that doesn't cast judgement (like in the wilderness) or among peers (chaos worshippers or a secret cabal of doomed heroes like the Characters).

The Players should be aware that they’re in for a journey into the dark, perhaps even as champions of Chaos. Interaction with society could be achieved by granting access to useful mutations, talents, illusionist spells, spectacular disguise kits or NPC proxies that the Players role-play during the social encounters. This supplement will serve you well on the Character’s descent into darkness as they ac:uire trivial, minor and major mutations.

Original material: "The Mutant's Handbook" by Anders Hellspong

Are you a mutant, or do you know someone who is? Then The Mutant’s Handbook is for you!  The Mutant’s Handbook is an unofficial supplement to WFRP 4e that provides variety, progressive severity of mutations and a slightly different take on mental mutations.

Variety: The Handbook contains different types of mutations with over  possible specific mutations. You should be able to find your favourites from the 2nd Edition Tome of Corruption as well as plenty of new exciting alterations for the up and coming mutant.

Progressive severity: This supplement provides a system where the first few mutations are likely to be trivial or minor, and hopefully possible to conceal - prolonging their ability to act within civilised society. Further mutation increases the risks becoming more and more severe with the rate of corruption.  The system is meant to support storylines of a gradual decline into corruption where the tainted try to conceal their shameful alterations and dark secrets from the people around them, or face becoming pariah.

New take on mental mutation: While mental mutations will most certainly make you insane, they are caused by Chaotic corruption of the mind, not mental illness. This supplement has no ambition of representing real-life mental illness. The ambition is to capture the inevitable terror of having your own mind betray you as a result of corruption. New desires, perspectives, behaviours and powers await the corrupted.

The way you deal with corruption in the setting of your game will greatly determine how to use this supplement.
